Dim the vertical rail to steel above and below the lit stretch from box to board. Consider giving the title a question form (see titles).

Keep the Now/Next/Later spine and the big-figure Coming up rows. Set the Now/Next/Later plates in the text face rather than tracked mono pills. Collapse Finish setting up to t3-pocket-graft's one-line '3 steps · Next: …' so To do rises to the top right. Graft t3-pocket-mut's rule that Vera's words glow and the family's stay matte, in Chat.

Its machine-voice glow (Vera's chat bubbles lit, the family's matte) is the most faithful return of the original light. Carry it to the lineage's best rather than as a standalone, and fix the inherited amber '6 worth a look' alarm on Status.
Drop the Victor Mono cursive pencil, which reads as a costume, and the navy who-tag chips. Keep the one-line setup stop and To do beside the box.

a.titles: Best: "What's our plan?" (t3-track-refine, t3-timetable-refine, t3-pocket-refine, t3-timetable-mut). It is short, a question in the family's own 'our', its lit word is the job, and it fits any phone. Close second: "Tell Vera our plans." (t3-timetable-graft). It names who hears you and the job, but it is an imperative with a full stop, so it reads as an instruction rather than an invitation, and 'plans' assumes they already exist. "What's the plan?" (refine2) works but loses the family's voice. "What needs planning?" (track-graft) is good wording, but the 8-letter lit word is heavy and its glow block dominates. "What should we plan?" sounds hesitant. "Anything to plan?" can be answered 'no' and is too casual. "What are we planning?" reads as a status check, not an invitation to tell her something.

b.notes: This heat answers the owner's 'nearly identical' complaint well. Figure and console now differ from today down the whole page, not in a corner. Grafted features that worked: Fig. 0's wired household (the owner's line language plus real phosphor plus the family's data; the best graft in the heat). Console-graft's day numeral carried from route ring to row to month cell (one mark threaded through every page). Its placards and pilot-lamp ticks. Switchboard-graft's radar set behind the question on the glass. Grafts that did not work: switchboard-graft's green Row 0 service lines on every inner page, which push the page back toward monochrome; console-mut's landscape picture, decoration that pretends to be data; switchboard-mut's squaring, which cannot be seen. On the light: figure-refine/graft and console-graft bring the halo back on the tubes, the lit ring and NOW, and the glow stays off the rest of the page, which is what the owner asked. On colour: bone, sky, slate-cyan, clay and amber-for-late all support the green rather than compete with it. Console-graft's bone route is the only one near the tan the owner dislikes. The switchboard lineage stays the greenest (58-73%) and has the least line art, so it most needs the rail and patch-cord lines.

scores.why: Matrix-green everywhere (83% green share), every box glows the same, no grounded companion and no structure-drawing line. 'What's on your mind?' is the title the owner rejected.
Calm and well built, with a real tube on Home. But the page is a grid of near-identical slate cards with little line art, and it keeps 'What's on your mind?'.
The railed manual already works: the Coming up rail with its lit NOW, bone ink, blueprint figures. But the Next up tube repeats the rail, and the tube light is thinner than the original's.

The rails are now held on every page: a lit NOW on Home, To do and the Plans weeks. The tubes are relit (countdown, round gauges) and amber is kept to late, all on calm green-black and bone. The 'Next in 2 days' tube still says what the rail beside it says, and the chat's sequence figure is a thin grey strip.

Fig. 0 is the best new element in the heat. The household is wired to Vera's blooming screen, the speaker's wire is lit, and terminals run out to 4 plans, 4 to do, 3 late, 12 ideas, wishes. It is the owner's line art, real CRT glow and the family's own data in one figure. It replaces the duplicate tube, and the rest stays grounded in bone, sky and clay, so the page reads very differently from today across its whole height.

The magazine setting is a real typographic gain: light display heads closing up as they grow, and small-cap datelines. The owner enjoys exactly this kind of work. But the light heads lose mass against the semibold rows, and the 12px caps labels ('VERA FRIDAY 2 OCTOBER', the column heads) feel faint.

The flight plan arcs, the readout rail with its dotted leaders and the master caution give Home a real instrument structure and grounded slate. The violet route reads off-period, and the caution is crowded on one line.

The box now leads, the caution reads in two clean lines, and the route is a calm slate-cyan with 'in 2 days' callouts. Every page gets one tube (the To do tube is new), and Status's annunciator lamps read well. The rows are numbered 1-3 with the next plan only in the tube, which loses the day as the key fact.

Waypoint lamps tie the page together. The day numeral sits in each route ring (the next one lit green and haloed), leads each Coming up row in light Plex, and heads each month cell. Pilot-lamp ticks run on To do, crew filters, and placards say how to read each tube. Bone grease-pencil route on slate, amber only for late, and the phosphor only on what is live: this is the owner's brief carried page by page.

A landscape drawn behind the question is literal decoration. It is fixed to one region, its violet legs look like data that disagrees with the real route, and text runs over it. The colour badges for kinds are a small win, and the one arrow family is tidy but invisible at page scale.

The sommaire map of the whole service is a strong idea, and the terminal glass has real phosphor. But the page is green-heavy (71%), and the green-on-green question plus the 3-digit page numbers keep it close to today's Matrix feel.

The most settled switchboard. Matte graphite racks, sky-numbered Plans with a small scope beside them, sea To do, a bone household foot, and the green pulled back to 58%. Each inner page opens on its own small tube (the To do bars, the Plans weekend) on a consistent rack. It has little line art, and the panels are boxy and similar.

The radar behind 'What's the plan?' on the glass is real phosphor, and the patch keys ('→ Plans', '→ To do') are a clever circuit idea. But green Row 0 banners on every inner page push green share back to 68%, the dashed caps add noise, and the household rack is ragged.
Squaring the lamps and glass is barely visible. The wiring went back to graphite, so green share rose to 73% and the leaders are faint. It is a near-duplicate of its parent at page scale.

fixes.suggestion: Keep Fig. 0, the household wired to Vera with the lit speaker's wire, and keep the lit-NOW rails on Coming up, To do and the Plans weeks, the bone/sky/clay inks and amber-only-for-late. Fix Fig. 0: let it grow with the data (fluid geometry, not fixed pixels) and make each terminal a real link that lands on its section; give its scanlines and bloom a touch more of the original strength so it reads as THE tube. Home: the Caution strip floats with a large empty left cell; set it into the rail's margin column or make it a two-line plate like console-refine's. Kids' wishes with '0 open' rows is dead weight; collapse it to one line when empty. Chat: the sequence figure is thin and grey, so give it the same lit newest arrow at full glow and let its lanes align with the message rows. Status: move the spend gauge into the wiring figure's tube so the page has one screen. Drop '#n' ids on Ideas to match Home.

Keep the day numerals carried from the route rings to the rows to the month cells, the lit next-ring with halo, the pilot-lamp ticks, the readout rail with its dotted leaders, the placards, and Status's annunciator. Fix: the bone route reads a touch warm/tan against the owner's dislike of tan. Cool it toward pewter-bone or console-refine's slate-cyan while keeping the dotted flown trail. Home: fill the empty ground right of Coming up's relative column (the calendar note is lonely there); move it under the rows and widen the titles. Unify the ring numerals with the row numerals (one face). The To do pilot lamps for late rows should glow amber, not sit as grey discs with a bar. Ideas: the readout tiles (Ideas 12, Places to eat 2) are small; fold them into the radar tube's placard. Plans: the month's route line across each week row is lovely; give the lit leg the full halo.

Keep the box-first Home, the two-line caution, the To do tube and slate-cyan route. Restore the day numeral in the Coming up rows (lead with 'Sun 4 Oct' including the next plan) instead of bare 1-2-3 counters; take console-graft's lit day ring on the route.

Keep the rails on every page and the relit round gauges on Plans and Status. Replace Home's duplicate 'Next in 2 days' tube with figure-graft's Fig. 0. To do's Fig. 1 tally dots are good; keep them. Close Plans' ~90px empty band under the gauge.

Graft its type into the lineage winner selectively: tightened display tracking and the light large page titles (Ideas, Plans, Status, Things to do) work beautifully. But keep section heads on Home at 500-600 weight so they carry mass, and raise the small-cap labels to 12.5-13px.

Keep the sommaire map, sky Plans / sea To do / bone household section inks, the small scope beside the plan rows, and the per-page rack with its own tube. Add line art: run a thin patch-cord track from each map cell's lamp to its count, and give the Plans rows a vertical timetable rail with a lit NOW (borrow the figure lineage's rail). Reduce the green on the question glass: set 'What's the' in bone, light only 'plan'. Lose the boxed empty month cells' heaviness (hairlines only).

Keep the radar on the question's glass and the patch keys naming their destination page. Drop the green Row 0 banner on inner pages, or set it in bone with one lit figure, so green share falls back under 55%.

b.titles: The two best are 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure-refine and figure-mut) and 'Tell Vera our plans.' (figure-graft). Each names who hears you and the job, invites the family to tell her something, and lights the job word at the end where the eye stops. 'Our plans' adds the family's voice and echoes the placeholder. 'Tell Vera our plan.' (console-graft) is close, but the singular reads slightly stiff. 'What's our plan?' (console-refine) has the family voice, but as a question it can read as 'show me the plan', and 'What are we planning?' (console-mut) reads the same way. Both are acceptable. 'What's the plan?' (switchboard-refine and switchboard-graft) is casual and kitchen-table, but it reads most like asking to be shown something rather than telling Vera. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard-mut) fails: it invites a yes/no. All of them beat 'What's on your mind?'.

b.notes: Through the soul lens, this round brought back real tubes in all three lineages. The switchboard brings back the most of the original light (glass, VT323, a cursor, a tube per page) and now keeps it to the tubes, so Settled Light leads. Figure Ground's Fig. 0 is the best new idea: phosphor that shows who spoke last. Grafts that worked: Fig. 0's wired household (from the switchboard and presence ideas); the switchboard's patch keys lighting a jack, and its Row 0 teletext line (good, but wrapping and too green); the console's waypoint numerals and pilot-lamp ticks (good, lamps where hands go). Grafts that did not work: Row 0 as a green banner on every page, and the console mutant's engraved landscape behind the question, which is decoration without light. Measures are consistent with what the screenshots show: switchboard green share is still high (57–72%), while figure and console sit near 40–47% with low neon in their other colours. The mutants (magazine type, square glass, drawn landscape) all lowered the soul. Light display type thins the halo, square glass loses the tube's silhouette, and the line art fights the glass.

scores.why: This is the original light at full strength: halo on every word, bloom on every panel. The soul is all there, but it is spent everywhere, so it reads as glare and Matrix rather than as light that means something.

The greeting is a real terminal: lit VT323 words on glass, the cursor and the Next up tube inside one case. Away from the glass it goes rather quiet and flat, so the light lives on Home's top left and not much further.
A calm, well-set manual with lit rails and a small Next up tube. The light is correct but thin. The tubes are small, and the phosphor reads as an accent more than as a monitor.

The tubes are switched back on. Home's countdown tube, the round Plans and Status gauges with bloom, the radar, and lit NOW rails on every list in time. Bone heads with a single haloed 'plan' make a lovely restrained key word. The light lands only where the machine is live.

Fig. 0 is the most alive thing in the heat: the household wired to Vera's blooming glyph screen on green glass, with the wire of whoever spoke last lit. That is phosphor carrying meaning, not decoration. On the phone, S A M T over her glowing screen is the original's soul in a new form. The round spend tube and the lit NOW rails hold it on the inner pages.

Light display heads and small caps turn the manual into a magazine. 'plan' at 64px light still glows, but the halo is weaker on thin strokes, and the page reads editorial rather than as a lit instrument. The tubes are unchanged from the parent.
A strong console grammar: the Next up tube, the readout strip and a lit live leg. But the box sits second behind the tube, and the violet-ish route and boxed panels dilute the lamp feeling.

Her box leads, with only 'plan' lit. The Next up tube beside it, the glowing Today readout, a lit leg and Now needle on the route, a real meter tube on Status and one tube on every page, To do's 'nothing dated ahead' included. The flight-log chat lights only the newest stop. Calm night-shift console, light where live.

Waypoint rings that carry the day numeral, with the next plan's numeral and its leg lit. Pilot-lamp ticks, amber for late, are lamps people actually press, which is phosphor where the hands go. The Status meter is the best instrument in this lineage. Weaknesses: the Plans head tube is small, and the bone route is a little faint.

The steel line-drawn landscape behind the question is an engraving, not a tube: it fights the text and has no light of its own beyond one green window. Its violet legs read as false data. The rest is the parent unchanged.

The question is typed on the glass in VT323, with a cursor and a radar inside one terminal case, which is pure original soul. But green share stays high (71%), and the household rack leans on green, so it is closer to the old glare.

The best recovery of the original light in this heat. 'What's the plan?' is lit on the glass over a recessed box with a '>' prompt, and every inner page opens on its own summary tube: To do's block tally, Plans' 'This weekend' screen, Ideas' radar '10 of 12', Status's spend screen. Halo, scanlines and breathing lamps are back at full strength, but only in those tubes, with matte graphite and bone everywhere else.

'What's the' dim and 'plan' white-hot under a three-layer halo, beside the radar on the glass, is a beautiful key word. The Row 0 videotex service lines are authentically teletext and make every page head a lit screen. The patch keys lighting a jack on the map are a lovely idea of light as connection. Weaknesses: Row 0 wraps on Ideas and To do and turns into a glowing bar across the top of every page, which drifts toward green everywhere (68% share).

A near duplicate of Patched. The square glass and lamps are faithful to videotex cells but cost the tubes their curved silhouette, and the faint leaders and higher green share make the glow less meaningful, not more.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit VT323 question on glass, the per-page summary tube in the 22rem column, and the matte graphite and bone everywhere else. That is the right split of light. Fix: (1) Home's household foot (Wishes, Memory, Family, Status, Settings) is the dimmest strip on the page. Give each cell a small breathing lamp, and light only the one that needs a look (Settings in amber, already partly there) so the sommaire is lit as a map. (2) The chat page has no tube. Light the newest Vera slip's edge with the afterglow, or put a small presence screen in the left column, so the chat keeps the light. (3) Cut green share: the textarea's inner glow and Vera's glyph screens are the biggest green areas. Keep the halo on the question text and the caret, and take the box's interior glow down by half. (4) To do's tube says 'Nothing dated after the late ones'. When something is due next, name it in white-hot. When nothing is, light the Late row's blocks amber-on-green so the tube still carries the news. (5) Restore the starters on the phone. They are the way in.

Keep Fig. 0 (the household wired to Vera's blooming screen, the speaker's wire lit) as the lineage's signature, along with the bone heads, the single haloed 'plans', and the lit NOW rails on Home, Plans and To do. Fix: (1) Let Fig. 0's lit wire breathe slowly (2–3s) and give her glyph screen faint scanlines, so it reads as a live tube, not a diagram on green. (2) Make Fig. 0 data-driven in width so that six members or 'next in 2 weeks' never clip. (3) The Plans countdown ring and the Status spend ring are good tubes. Give the Ideas radar the same bezel and power-on, so all three inner tubes are one family. (4) The chat sequence diagram should light the newest arrow and its sender's monogram node with the same halo as Fig. 0's wire, linking Home and Chat. (5) The Caution line on Home floats. Put a small amber lamp in its ring that breathes, and keep the rest matte.

Keep the 'Next in 2 days' tube, the round gauges, and one lit NOW per list. Fix the visible gap in the month's NOW trace across Mon to Thu: carry it as a dim afterglow line to today's outline. Make the To do Fig. 1 counters tiny lamps (amber for late) with the halo, so the figure is lit as well as drawn.

Keep the dim-plus-white-hot question, the radar on the glass, and the patch keys that light a jack. Those are light-as-meaning. Fix: (1) Row 0 must never wrap. Shorten it to one line per page (e.g. 'Late 3 · next: Call the dentist'), or let it truncate with an ellipsis. (2) Make Row 0 a dark glass strip with only its one figure white-hot, not a green-tinted bar, so each page head is a tube and not a green banner. (3) Fill the empty dotted cell in the household rack, or remove it. (4) Bring back Refine's per-page summary tubes on Plans and To do instead of the Row 0 alone, or make Row 0 the tube's top line.

Keep the box first, the Next up tube beside it, the readout strip with a lit Today, and the meter tube on Status. Fix: (1) The route on Home is faint slate-cyan. Light the flown-to-next leg with a real halo and let the Next ring breathe, so the flight plan has one lamp. (2) The To do 'nothing dated ahead' tube is two lines on a big glass. Add a lit late count or a crew-board row of lamps. (3) Lately added's tiny swatches feel flat. Keep them, but give the newest item a fading afterglow edge.

Keep the waypoint rings carrying the day numeral (the next one lit), the pilot-lamp ticks and the big Status meter. Fix: make the bone route a little stronger and the flown trail clearly dotted. Grow the Plans head tube so it matches Status's. Unify the ring numerals with the row numerals (one face).

Drop the line-drawn landscape behind the text. If a picture is wanted, draw it as a phosphor vector on the Next up tube (hills in dim green scanline, the home window lit), not as steel engraving inside the box. Keep the unified solid arrowheads only if they are lit green on the primary links.

b.titles: The best are 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure refine and mutant) and 'Tell Vera our plans.' (figure graft). Both name who hears you, say the job as an invitation to tell her something, end on the lit word where the eye stops, and fit one phone line. 'What's the plan?' (switchboard) is the strongest on the glass: short, the family's own breakfast question, and it suits a VT323 prompt with 'plan' white-hot. But it reads as 'show me the plan' rather than 'tell her', so it is better as the terminal's prompt than as an invitation. 'What's our plan?' (console refine) has the same weakness with a warmer 'our'. 'Tell Vera our plan.' (console graft) is fine but singular, so it presumes one plan. 'What are we planning?' (console mutant) is warm, but the long lit word carries less halo. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard mutant) fails: it is a yes/no question you can answer 'no' to, and it is the least inviting.

b.notes: Grafts that worked: Fig. 0 in Wired Household. It is a feature built in the lineage's own terms, and it answers the owner's 'reflect the page content' with a picture of the household itself. The day-numeral system and placards in Waypoint Lamps worked too. In Patched Through, Row 0 and the patch keys suit videotex perfectly. Grafts that did not: Waypoint's ring numerals in mono beside sans rows, and Patched Through's household rack, which loses alignment. The phosphor returns most convincingly in the switchboard glass (VT323, radar, bloom) and in figure-graft's Fig. 0. The figure lineage keeps the best balance between grounded colour and light. Mutants: Magazine's display type is the one worth harvesting. Drawn's landscape has charm but needs to be made generic. Squared is a near-duplicate. Across lineages, the strongest synthesis would be the figure-graft Home with switchboard's Row 0 headers on inner pages and the console's day-numeral rows.

scores.why: Fig. 0, the household wired to Vera's blooming glyph screen with the last speaker's wire lit, is the most memorable new picture in the heat. It is the manual's promise kept on Home, and the rule that every mark in a figure links to its row turns the conceit into a system. Bone condensed heads on green-black read as a well-printed manual lit by one tube.

The calmest, best-set version of the manual: one rule on every page (a figure touches its rows, a lit NOW per list), with real tubes on the Plans and Status gauges. The Home tube ('Next in 2 days') is less distinctive than the graft's Fig. 0, so its identity rests on the rails.

The day numeral used as one mark across Coming up rows, waypoint rings and month cells is a real typographic idea, and the flight-plan arcs with a lit leg, the pilot-lamp ticks and the placards make the 1969 console read as a coherent instrument panel rather than a costume.

The page most like the original tube: VT323 'What's the plan?' on glass, with the radar inside the greeting. The Row 0 videotex service line heading each inner page is the freshest header idea in the heat. The patch keys under the box (→ Plans, → To do) say where a message goes. The green share is still high, and the glass is underfilled around the title.

The sommaire map is the clearest 'whole service on one screen' idea, and putting a small scope beside the plan rows it numbers is lovely. The household rack across the foot works. The inner pages' side tubes (the spend meter, To do's ASCII bar) have charm. Graphite plates make it read a little like a dashboard.

Light sentence-case display heads and small-cap labels give the manual an editorial elegance, and 'Things to do' and 'Plans' at display size feel like a magazine spread. The light heads lose mass on the squint, though, and the green key and the semibold rows now outrank them.

Clean and well paced, with the readout rail, the two-line caution and the slate-cyan route. Dropping the next plan from the numbered list (rings 1, 2, 3 after an unnumbered Next) makes the plot harder to read, and the page is quieter than the graft without being more distinctive.

The drawn night country under the question, with home's one lit window, is the most charming single picture here and could get an 'oh, that's lovely'. But it is regional and hard-coded, its violet legs read as false data, and it sits behind the words people type.
A solid railed manual, now surpassed by its refinement and its graft on the light and on the Home figure.
The base console idea, with faults its children clear: the violet route and a muddled caution line.
A strong map structure, but very green (71% of the colour) and boxy, with tracked VT323 'Anything to plan?' and small leaders.
Squaring the lamps and blips is a coherent videotex thought, but it is a near-duplicate at page scale, and it brings the parent's green back up.
The original glow has charm, but the page is a monochrome wash with no structure of its own: 'the Matrix'.
A well-made desk terminal with good grounded colour, but its identity is a refined terminal card rather than a memorable idea drawn from the family's data.

fixes.suggestion: Keep Fig. 0, the lit last-speaker wire, the rule that a mark links to its row, the bone condensed heads and the title. Fix the following. In Fig. 0, draw '3 late' as an amber lamp, not a green-highlighted cell, since amber means late everywhere else; draw member monograms larger, with the grown-up/kid bone/heather split visible, and make Fig. 0 lay out by data (members N, terminal widths) rather than fixed pixels. The Caution row sits in an empty left column with a lot of black: give it the same figure column as the rows below, or fold it into the glass's foot. Bring the refine's real Plans gauge (with the halo) to Status' spend tube as well, so the tubes share one grammar. Lately added is the only section with no figure: a small kind tally or a dot strip would keep the rule true on every section.

Graft Fig. 0 from Wired Household onto Home in place of the 'Next in 2 days' tube, which repeats Coming up. Keep the Plans and Status round gauges with their halo, the To do NOW rail and the amber counters. On Plans Month, close the ~90px gap by moving the Next line under the gauge's caption. The month NOW trace that breaks across Mon to Thu should run through to today's outline.

Its display heads are worth carrying into the winner as page titles only ('Plans', 'Things to do', 'Status' at light 300 with tight tracking). Keep the section heads (Coming up, To do) semibold condensed so the squint keeps its hierarchy, and drop the hand-scaled small caps under 12px.

Keep the day numeral as one mark (rows, waypoint rings, month cells), the lit leg, pilot-lamp ticks and placards. Fix the following. Set the ring numerals in the same Plex Sans 300 as the rows, so one mark has one face. Fill the empty ground right of Coming up's relative column: move the 'not connected' note there as a placard, or widen the titles. On Plans Month, the arc lines between cells are thin and read as noise: thicken the route ahead and make the dotted flown trail fainter. The chat's flight-log spine with a lit last stop is good; give Vera's lit box less green fill. On To do, make the crew line read as lamps rather than a link row.
Number the next plan too (or drop the numbers), so the arcs and rows agree. Take the graft's day-numeral rows instead of the mono date column.

The drawn horizon is worth keeping as an optional, data-free emblem: make it generic (low hills, a road and a lit home window), drop the violet legs that mimic data, put it in the glass's lower-right corner clear of the typing area, and draw it in the palette's tokens (inline SVG with currentColor) so it themes.

Keep the VT323 title on glass with the radar, the Row 0 service lines on inner pages (the best inner-page header in the heat) and the patch keys with their destinations. Fix the following. Lower the green share by setting the glass's dim words, Vera's chat slips and the leaders in bone or steel, so that green stays on 'plan', the lamps and the figures. Fill the glass's empty space by putting the date and the next plan's one line under the title. Row 0 wrapping to two lines on Ideas and To do: shorten it to one line (count · nearest · furthest) with no orphan separator. The household rack in the right column aligns to nothing: give its cells the same column edges as the Plans and To do rows above.

Keep the two-tier sommaire, the small scope beside the plan rows, the household rack across the foot and the inner rack of plate, primary and tube. Graft in the Row 0 service line from Patched Through as each inner page's header. Raise the dotted leaders one step in contrast. Show 'Continue with Vera' and one starter on the phone. The To do cell's 80px empty foot should shrink to its content.

b.titles: The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure-refine and figure-mut). It names who hears you and the whole job in one verb, invites a message, and lands its lit word at the full stop. 'Tell Vera our plans.' (figure-graft) is a close second: warm and in the family's own 'our', matching Fig. 0's household, though the plural reads a little like a report. 'What's the plan?' (switchboard) is the family's own kitchen-table voice, but it reads as 'show me the plan' rather than 'tell her'. 'What's our plan?' and 'Tell Vera our plan.' (console) are good but flatter versions of the above. 'What are we planning?' (console-mut) is pleasant but generic. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard-mut) fails: it is a yes/no question that invites 'no'.

b.notes:
The Figure Ground lineage now has the strongest system in the heat. Its single rule, a figure that touches its rows and a rail with one lit NOW, holds on Home, To do, Plans, Status and Settings, so it would define a standard for any page.

Grafts that worked:
- Fig. 0's wired household: real data, and the page's personality.
- The console's single day numeral across rows, rings and month.
- The switchboard's starters keyed to their destination pages.
- The Row 0 service line as a compact head.

Grafts that did not work:
- The console-mut landscape: decoration that misstates data, under typed text.
- The switchboard-mut squaring: invisible, and it made the page greener.
- The dashed separated-block caps: noise.

The console lineage's main system fault is boxes in boxes. The switchboard's is the narrow inner-page rack and the high green share. Bringing back the phosphor light is done best by figure-refine's round tubes and lamps: light where the machine is live, bone and slate elsewhere.

scores.why: One rounded green card style and one green ink for everything. There is no hierarchy of surfaces and no colour with a job. The page reads as the Matrix and gives a system little to build on.

A disciplined desk-terminal system: steel caps, one contents rail, small tubes. It is coherent on every page but quieter and more uniform than the best of this heat. Its figures say less about the page's content.
The manual grammar is already strong: a figure column, rails, a bone ink and a blueprint ink with jobs. The light is thin, and Status's figure floats free of its rows.

The most complete system in the heat. Every page opens with a figure in the left column that touches its rows. Every time list hangs from a rail with one lit NOW (Home, To do, Plans weeks). The round countdown and spend gauges are real tubes again, and amber, sky and bone each keep to one job. It reads the same on Plans, To do, Status and Settings, and the greeting is clean and calm.

Fig. 0, the household wired to Vera's screen, is the best new Home idea in the heat and draws real data. But its pixel-fixed geometry, the S/A/M/T letters set at display size and the narrowed box make the greeting busier. The kid heather and the one rail-date ink are good system rules. Status's lamp words in faint grey beside the lamps are an improvement.

The magazine typesetting is genuinely nicer to read: 300-weight sentence-case display heads with tightened tracking, small-cap datelines and legends. But light heads lose their mass on the squint, so the semibold rows and the green outrank the section heads. It changes how the system reads more than what it shows.
A strong readout rail and an arcing flight plan. The bays are heavy, the caution is crowded into one line, and the violet route reads as a costume colour.

One day numeral used everywhere (Coming up rows, waypoint rings, month cells) is a real system rule, and the warm bone route on slate is grounded. The pilot-lamp ticks and placards also hold across pages. But every block is a bay inside a bay, so the page is box-heavy. Status's amber 'Needs a look' readout and the big meter crowd the head.

Execution is cleaner: the box leads, a two-line caution and a slate-cyan route. But taking the next plan out of the Coming up list (the rows start at ①) is confusing. The slim flight-plan arcs are faint, and the To do tube saying 'nothing dated ahead' spends a tube on nothing.

The hard-coded volcano-and-fir landscape behind the question is decoration that draws a route which isn't the data. It also sits under the words the family types. The badge kinds and the unified arrowheads are fine, but small at page scale.
The sommaire map is a clear Home structure. But it is very green (71%), the inner pages are cramped into a narrow left rack, and the VT323 'Anything to plan?' reads as a yes/no.

A settled two-tier map. Plans and To do are a step larger, a scope sits beside the plan rows it numbers, and the household strip has counts. Each inner page has one rack plus a small tube with a job, such as To do's late/this week/later meter. Typographic rhythm and the leaders are good. The tube glass on Home is smaller, so the phosphor feels reduced to the inset prompt. The 22rem rack leaves Plans' month and To do's list floating short.

Keying each starter to the page it lands on ('→ Plans', '→ To do') is a clever circuit idea. The one-line Row 0 service bar on inner pages is compact and informative. But the dashed separated-block caps everywhere add noise, the green share is still high, and Row 0 wraps. The Home household block also aligns to nothing.
Squaring the lamps and blips is near-invisible at page scale. Returning the wiring to graphite made the page greener and the leaders fainter, a step back on the owner's grounded-colour test.

fixes.suggestion:
Keep: the figure-left/rows-right rack on every page, the one lit NOW per rail, the round tubes on Plans and Status, and the amber/sky/bone job rules. Fix:
- Plans Month: close the 90px dead band by putting the Next line beside the gauge and starting the grid under it. Carry the month's NOW trace through today's cell rather than stopping at the grid edge.
- Home: put Coming up's NOW and To do's Now tick at one height, or make To do's an unlabelled tick, so the two rails don't compete.
- Status: move 'Working/Off' words into the lamp colour's dim ink, not in a separate right-aligned column.
- Take Fig. 0's wired-household idea from the graft as a small figure on the Family page, not on Home.

Keep Fig. 0 (it draws real data and says who Vera serves), the heather kid ink and the one-ink-for-rail-dates rule. Fix:
- Set the S/A/M/T monograms at text size in bone, not 22px letters at the glass edge.
- Make the wire geometry an SVG with viewBox so it scales past five members.
- Give the box back its width: put Fig. 0 below the box on narrower widths, or limit it to 360px.
- Ideas: drop the '#n' ids from the Nearest/Furthest lines to match Home.

Keep the tracking per size and the small-cap legends; they are worth folding into the refine. Fix:
- Raise the section heads to 400 weight (light only for the page h1), so section heads keep their mass on the squint.
- Keep 13px as the smallest desktop text.

Keep the one day numeral across rows, rings and month cells, the bone route and the pilot-lamp ticks. Fix:
- Remove one level of bay: lists that are only read (To do, Lately added) should sit on the ground under a rule, not in boxes.
- Use one face for the numeral in the ring and in the row.
- Status: put the working/off/needs-a-look readout in one row beside the h1, and move the meter under it so the head isn't stacked.
- Fill the empty right side of the Coming up rows with the relative date, or narrow the bay.

Keep the two-line caution and the readout rail. Put the next plan back as row 1 in Coming up (lit), so the list and the route agree. Make the route arcs 1.5px with the flown part dotted. Drop the To do tube when nothing is dated ahead.

Keep the two-tier sommaire and the household counts strip, which is the best Home map. Fix:
- Make the Home glass larger, with the scope inside it, so the phosphor has a real screen on Home.
- Widen the inner-page rack's list column, or put the tube above the list on Plans and To do so short lists don't float.
- Graft the graft's '→ Plans / → To do' patch keys onto the starters, and its Row 0 as an optional single line, not wrapping.

Keep the patch keys and Row 0. Remove the dashed separated-block caps (one solid 2px cap is enough), and cut Row 0 to one line at 1280. Bring back grounded section inks in the frames to lower the green share.

b.titles: The best title is "Tell Vera what to plan." (figure refine and mutant). It names who hears you and gives the job as one verb at the end of the line, where the glow lands, and it is an imperative invitation that fits a phone. Close behind is "Tell Vera our plan(s)." (console graft, figure graft): 'our' is warm, but "our plans" reads slightly like a report rather than an invitation. "What's our plan?" and "What are we planning?" work as kitchen-table questions but are narrower, and they could be read as asking the app to show a plan. "What's the plan?" (switchboard) reads most like 'show me the plan', the opposite of telling her. "Anything to plan?" fails: it invites a yes/no and doesn't say Vera does the planning.

b.notes: Across the heat the basics are solved: every candidate has zero targets under 44px except Settled Light (one, on Home and on the phone), and the Tab order is identical to today's (skip, bar, box, select, mic, Send). So the lens comes down to sight lines and how much a figure helps rather than repeats. What worked: Waypoint Lamps' shared day numeral (from the main tournament's date-led rows) is the strongest graft, because it ties figure to list with no legend. Patched Through's destination tags on the starters are the best wording-level comprehension gain. Wired Household's one-line Caution strip beats every two-panel setup block. What did not work: Wired Household's S/A/M/T wiring figure is a cryptic decoration in the first screen. Waypoint Lamps' round checkboxes trade a clear control for a motif. Drawn's landscape behind the input and its decorative legs mislead. Squared's square lamps blur into square checkboxes. Figure Ground's chat sequence-diagram panel and Fig. 1 date grid still duplicate the list beside them, which costs width without adding information. The yardsticks: today's page is far behind on targets and title, and Desk Terminal, Joined, sits about level with the best of this heat; Waypoint Lamps edges past it on comprehension.

scores.why: Clear enough to read, but 42 targets on Home are under 44px, the starters are small pills, and the title 'What's on your mind?' doesn't say what the box is for. On the squint the Next up tube outweighs the box.

No small targets, and it reads tube, then box, then a dense right column. The tube sits above the question, so the eye lands on the next plan before the action, and the right column is dense at a glance.
The eye goes title, box, Send. The rail with its lit NOW reads at once, and the phone's keys ('3 more plans / 4 to do / 3 late') are good. The Fig. 1 grid repeats dates the rows already show.

The best sight line in its lineage: a big imperative title, one box, a lit Send, then Coming up and To do hung from the same lit NOW. To do's NOW tick under the late rows shows at once what is overdue. The left grid still spends 300px repeating the dates, the chat's sequence-diagram panel is a small duplicate of the thread, and the next plan appears twice (in the tube and in row 1).

The one-line Caution strip and the single-column Lately added are the clearest in the heat. But Fig. 0 is hard to read: the single letters S/A/M/T and 'Alex Sun 19:52' need the caption to decode. On the phone the figure takes the first screen's second half where the next plan used to be.
The interaction is the parent's. The light sentence-case heads lose mass on the squint, so the semibold rows and the green key pull harder than the section heads, and the page is taller for it.
The readout rail is excellent: Today, Plans, To do, Late and Ideas read in one glance. Icon-only Send on the phone, and on desktop the tube to the left of the question pulls the eye before the box.

The box now leads, the leader readout rail is clear, and the two-line caution names the next step as a link. But the next plan has been taken out of the list: the rows are numbered 1-3 from Mount St. Helens while the route's 'Next' stop has no row, so the numbering and the route disagree. The flight plan also leaves a large empty strip beside the list.

The best comprehension device in the heat: one light day numeral (4, 9, 17, 24) sits in the route's ring and leads the row, so the figure and the list read as one thing without a legend. The placard under the tube says how to read it, the readout rail and the one-line caution are clean, and the lit Next row stands out. Its fault is the controls: every checkbox is a round 'pilot lamp', so ticked reads like a radio, and late rows show an amber minus in a circle that reads like 'remove' or 'disabled'.

The landscape sits behind the text you type. Its violet legs read as data that doesn't match the real flight plan below. Send is icon-only on the phone. The kind badges help scanning on Ideas, but the rest is the parent.

Home as a map of the pages is quick to scan. The VT323 'Anything to plan?' reads as yes/no, the phone puts the radar into the first screen, and most inner pages leave a large empty field below a short table.

The most findable Home: every page is a cell with its count, and Plans and To do are a step larger. On the phone the starters are full-width, with setup and Plans on the first screen. The tube on To do says 'Nothing dated after the late ones', which tells you little. Plans has no visible month name in the main area. One target on Home is still under 44px.

Each starter is labelled with where it lands (What should we do this weekend? → Plans; Remind me to… → To do; We should try… → Ideas), the clearest 'what will this do' signal anywhere in the tour. But the radar inflates the glass, which pushes the starters below a big tube on the phone, and the household rack ends in a hatched empty cell that reads as a broken control. Row 0 wraps with a dangling separator.

Interaction is the parent's, with fainter leaders, which are harder to follow on a dim screen. Square lamps and LEDs are less distinct from the square checkboxes, so state reads a little less clearly.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the day numeral as the shared key between ring and row (Home, Plans month), the placard under each tube, the readout rail and the one-line caution. Fix the controls: go back to a square checkbox well (a lamp may glow inside it when ticked) so a tick never reads as a radio. Draw late rows' boxes as an empty square with the amber 3px row edge, not an amber minus in a circle, which reads as 'remove'. Make the afterglow visible (it barely shows in the details strip). On the phone, bring the readout rail up into the first screen, for example by folding the tube's placard there.

Keep the box-first greeting with the label inside the frame and the two-line caution. Put the next plan back into the Coming up list as row 'Next' (lit) and number the route's rings to match the rows, so the figure and the list agree. Use the empty right of the flight plan for the Google note at row height rather than a floating column.

Keep the imperative title, the single rail with one lit NOW across Coming up and To do, the lamp grammar and the phone's key row. Give the 300px Fig. 1 grid a job the rows don't already do (a week density or free-weekend gaps), or narrow it to the rail itself so the list gets the width. Drop the duplicate next-plan line (tube or row 1, not both). In the chat, fold the sequence-diagram panel into the thread's own gutter rather than a separate mini-copy.

Keep the one-line Caution strip and the mark-links-to-its-row-and-lands-lit rule. Replace Fig. 0's single letters with names (or monogram plus name) and label the lit wire 'last spoke: Alex, 19:52'. On the phone, put the figure below Coming up rather than in the first screen.

Keep the sommaire Home (cells with counts, Plans and To do larger) and the full-width phone starters. Graft in Patched Through's destination tags on the starters (→ Plans / → To do / → Ideas). Show the month name in Plans' main area. Make To do's tube name the next task or the oldest late one rather than 'Nothing dated after the late ones'. Find and fix the last sub-44px target on Home.

Keep the starters' destination tags and the jack lighting on hover. Take the radar off the greeting glass (or shrink it to a lamp) so the title and box lead and the phone's first screen reaches the starters. Remove the hatched empty cell in the household rack. Keep Row 0 to one line at 1280, cutting the trailing separator.

b.titles: The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Figure Ground refine and mutant). It is an imperative invitation that names who hears you and the job in one verb, and the lit word falls where the eye stops. It reads as an instruction to type, which is what a box label should be. 'Tell Vera our plan.' and 'Tell Vera our plans.' come next: warm and the family's own voice, but they presume a plan already exists, and 'our plans' reads a little like 'report our plans'. 'What's our plan?' and 'What's the plan?' fail as labels: they ask the machine to show you the plan, which is the opposite of the box's job, and in the switchboard's VT323 the dim 'What's the' leaves only 'plan?' readable at a glance. 'What are we planning?' invites an answer and fits the job but is longer on a phone. 'Anything to plan?' reads as yes/no. Best one or two: 'Tell Vera what to plan.', then 'Tell Vera our plan.'

b.notes: Through the type lens, the Magazine mutant is the clearest advance. It changes the page's character everywhere (Home, Status, To do, Plans) with no change of colour, which answers the owner's 'reflect more of the page content'. It also shows that the Figure Ground lineage's manual idea wants a real type system, not more figures. Grafts that worked: console-graft's day numeral (a typographic feature carried across the route, the rows and the month), switchboard-graft's destination subscripts under the patch keys, and figure-graft's one-line Caution sentence. Grafts that did not: figure-graft's Fig. 0, whose spaced monograms and crowded VT323 compete with the title; and the switchboard's 3-digit page numbers, kept in two variants, which add noise before every head. VT323 titles in the switchboard line still mishandle the apostrophe. Across all three lineages, leaders with right-aligned tabular figures are now a shared and successful convention, worth adopting as a standard.

scores.why: Small mono-heavy body, tracked capitals on the date and the NEXT UP label, ISO dates in To do, a timid 15px question. Legible, but it has no type scale to speak of.

A consistent terminal type system with tabular mono columns that line up, but mono and tracked caps everywhere make it dense and samey. The greeting question is small, so there is little hierarchy between the title, the heads and the rows.
Condensed semibold heads over Plex rows, mono rail dates that align, a 52px title with its lit word. Solid, but the section heads and row titles sit close in weight.

A clear scale: a 52px condensed title, 22px condensed heads, 15px semibold rows. Rail dates are split as a dim weekday and a mono date, so the figures line up across Coming up. Fig. captions are set like a manual's, and the footer has a proper measure. The tube's VT323 'Next in 2 days' pairs well with the rest.

Keeps Relit Rails' type system and adds a good one-line Caution line with a sensible measure. Fig. 0's large spaced S A M T monograms and its crowded VT323 terminals fight the calm manual, and one long Lately added column loses the two-column rhythm.

The best typesetting in the heat. Light sentence-case display heads ('Status', 'What is working', 'Coming up') close up as they grow, small-cap labels (VERA · FRIDAY 2 OCTOBER, WHO ANSWERS, FIG. 1) are the only capitals, and the Status tallies are set as figure-plus-small-unit ('3 of 4', '$0.00 of $2.00'), which is genuinely magazine-grade. The hierarchy changes the look of every page, not a corner. Risks: light 30px heads are thin on 1x screens, and the jump from a 36px head to 15px rows is steep.
A good readout strip of tabular figures, but the title is buried mid-box and the label sizes are many and close together.

The readout rail is the best-set figure strip here: label, dotted leader, right-aligned tabular numeral. The box title is 36px condensed and the rail dates are mono columns. Lately added's inline small kind words beside bold titles make a ragged baseline, and the italic tagline in the footer is a nice touch.

The day numeral as one light figure (a large '4' with 'Oct/Sun' stacked small) is real calendar typesetting, and it repeats on the route, the rows and the month. The leaders and the two-line Lately added stacks keep good rhythm, and To do's figures are aligned. Minus: the ring numerals are mono 500 while the row numerals are sans 300, two faces for one mark.
Type is the parent's; the drawn hills sit under the field, so typed words run over a picture, and the 22px kind badges push up the card line-height against 13px labels.
A contents-page set of leaders and figures, but the VT323 'Anything to plan?' is small for a title, and the 3-digit page numbers add clutter in front of every head.

The household rack reads like a book's contents: head, dotted leader, a large light figure with its unit word in small ('4 coming', '12 saved'). The day numerals stack weekday and month cleanly. Minus: VT323 gives the apostrophe in 'What's' a whole cell, the title sits small on the glass, and To do leaves dead space.

Patch keys with a small destination line under each ('→ Plans') are a neat typographic idea, but 'What's the' is set dim in VT323 at low contrast, the apostrophe still gaps, Ideas has about 75px of empty column, and the copyright is set in tiny mono.

Swapping in the true Plex Sans Condensed cut where the parent faked width is a real if invisible improvement, and VT323 sets 'Anything to plan?' cleanly. Faint leaders and the 3-digit page numbers keep it busy.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the light sentence-case display heads, the small caps as the only capitals, and the figure-plus-small-unit tallies on Status; make that the lineage's type system. Fix: bring the section heads down one step (Coming up and To do 36px down to about 30px, with settings sub-heads at 300 → 350/400 weight) so the drop to the 15px rows is a scale, not a cliff. Raise the 12px small-cap labels to 12.5–13px, or draw them from Plex's real small-cap-like 500 weight, so they hold on 1x screens. Give the light heads a touch more mass on the squint with 400 below 32px. Carry the '3 of 4' tally treatment into Home's To do head ('4 · 3 late') and Plans' week counts.

Keep the 52px condensed title with 'plan' lit at the line's end, the weekday/date split on the rails and the Fig. captions. Graft the mutant's small caps for NOW, FIG. and the eyebrow labels in place of the mixed 'Now'/'NOW' settings. Make To do's NOW label match Coming up's (the same size and case). Put the Plans week ranges on the same mono tabular figures as Home's rail.

Keep the one-line Caution sentence and the 'Fig. 0' caption. Redraw Fig. 0's monograms at row-label size rather than 28px spaced capitals, and give the terminals one line each with consistent VT323 sizes. Bring Lately added back to two columns so its measure and rhythm match the sections above.

Keep the light day numeral with stacked month and weekday everywhere: it is the best date setting in the heat. Set the ring numerals in the same Plex Sans (tabular, 500) so one mark has one face. Right-align the 'in N days' column to a tab stop near the titles to close the gap after short titles. Keep the readout leaders.

Keep the readout rail (label, leader, tabular figure) and the in-box 36px title. In Lately added, put the kind word on a second line or in a fixed column, so the bold title and the 13px kind do not share a ragged baseline. Adopt the graft's day-numeral setting for the Coming up rows instead of the mono 'Fri 9 Oct' string.

Keep the contents-page leaders with large light figures and small unit words, and the stacked day numerals. Set the apostrophe in 'What's' in Plex, or use a VT323-safe title, and set the glass title at least 40px so it leads the page. Close To do's empty foot by letting the cell end with its rows. Darken the leaders a step so they read on a phone.

Keep the patch keys with their small destination lines. Set the whole title at full ink, with only 'plan' lit and 'What's the' not dimmed below body contrast. Fix the Row 0 wrap by shortening it or letting it break at a phrase rather than leaving a separator dot at the end of the first line. Set the copyright in the body sans, not tiny mono.

b.titles: The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure refine and mutant). It is an imperative sentence that names who hears you and gives the job in one verb, the lit word lands at the end where the eye stops, and it sets well both as a 52px condensed semibold title and as a 64px light one. Next is 'What's our plan?' (console refine): short, the family's own 'our', one phone line, and the lit word last. 'What are we planning?' (console mut) is warm but longer, and 'planning' is a heavier word to glow. 'Tell Vera our plan.' and 'Tell Vera our plans.' read slightly off ('tell her our plans' presumes a plan already exists). 'What's the plan?' reads as a request to be shown the plan rather than an invitation to tell her, and in VT323 its apostrophe takes a whole cell. 'Anything to plan?' is a yes/no question and the weakest invitation.

b.notes: Through the usability lens the heat splits on whether the signature graphic carries a task. Where it does, the page is easier than today's. Figure Refine's NOW rail on To do turns 'what is overdue' into one glance. Console's readout strip answers 'how are we doing' in one row. Switchboard's Home reaches every page with its count. Where the graphic is only a picture, it costs space or clarity: Fig. 0's S A M T letters, the console mutant's hills behind the text, and the arcs band above Coming up. Every candidate clears the 44px target floor except one stray target on switchboard-refine's Home (today's page has 42 small ones), and every candidate is at 12px or more, with the figure lineage at 13-14px. Grafts that worked: switchboard-graft's starter keys that say where they land; console-graft's leading day numeral, shared by the row, the ring and the month cell; figure-graft's two-line Caution strip, which is clearer than a banner. Grafts that did not: console-graft's pilot-lamp checkboxes, which break one-control-one-look; the To do ticks and the form's 'Needs booking' read as radio buttons or status lights. Also figure-graft's Fig. 0, which uses the phone's whole second screen to show initials, and switchboard-graft's dim 'What's the'. Removals: switchboard-refine hides two starters on the phone, a small real loss for a family that uses 'Remind me to…' from Home. Console-refine leaves the next plan out of Coming up's list, which keeps it only in the tube. Figure-refine's Late tab works only once the route supports it.

scores.why: Everything is there, but 42 targets on Home are under 44px, text goes down to 11.5px, To do is a grid of cards where 'overdue' is an ISO date in small grey type, and Home's order (setup, then wishes, then plans low down) hides the week.

No small targets, 12px floor, a clear desk layout with the box first and To do as Who/Due rows. Its narrow left console makes the chat's kids' conversations and To do's filters cramped, and the mono titles are harder to read on a phone.

Railed lists are easy to read (date, title, time, 'in 2 days'), late is amber with words, and text is 13px or larger. The Next tube on Home repeats the first rail row, and the figure column takes width on every page.

The easiest walk-through in the heat. 'Tell Vera what to plan.' sits over a wide box, and Coming up and To do each hang from one rail with a lit NOW, so overdue is simply 'above the line, amber, says Late'. To do gains a Late 3 tab, setup is a numbered checklist, settings list their state, and the text floor is the heat's highest (13-14px). The only costs are the figure gutter's width and the Late tab, which the route still ignores.

It keeps the railed lists and adds a two-line Caution strip. But Fig. 0's S A M T letters make no sense to a first-timer, take the whole first phone screen after the box, and duplicate counts that are said again below.

Same tasks and controls as its parent, but light headings lose their pull on a dim phone. The small-cap labels at 12px (KIND, DRIVE, ABOUT) are harder to scan than the parent's, and the taller heads push the lists down.
The readout strip gives the counts at a glance, but its labels are small, the flight-plan arcs are decoration a family must learn, and the caution banner is a single dense line.

The box comes first and the readout strip (Today, Plans 4, To do 4, Late 3, Ideas 12) answers 'how are we doing' at once. The caution now reads in two plain lines with the next step as a link, and To do keeps plain square checkboxes. The weakness: Coming up's list starts at the second plan, so the next plan lives only in the tube, and the arcs above the rows take space without adding a task.

Leading each Coming up row with a big day numeral is the clearest date treatment in the heat. But the ticks became round 'pilot lamps': To do's checkboxes and the form's 'Needs booking' box look like radio buttons or status lights, and late ones show a dash. A first-timer will not know they can tick them, which breaks one control, one look.

The parent's usability is unchanged on most pages, but the box now has hills drawn behind what you type. On the phone the box is taller and Send is icon-only, and the decorative violet legs over the box can be misread as plans.
Home as a map of every page with counts is a fast way in, but the green-on-glass VT323 question and box are lower contrast than plain type, and the side rack crowds the inner pages.

Home is a real map: Plans with day numerals and 'in 2 days', To do as Who/Due rows, Ideas with Restaurants · 2 to try, and a household row reaching Wishes, Memory, Family, Status and Settings, each with its count. Settings sorts 'Needs a look' to the top. The weaknesses: the VT323 'What's the plan?' reads less easily than plain type, the phone hides two of the three starters, and To do leaves empty graphite.

Starter keys that say where each lands (→ Plans, → To do) teach the app. But 'What's the' is dim on the glass, an unexplained hatched empty box sits beside Status, and Row 0 on Ideas and To do wraps and ends a line on a separator.
Same tasks as its parent, but the leaders are back at near-invisible graphite and the square lamps read more like checkboxes than status lights. It is a near-duplicate with a small legibility loss.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP the one-rail-with-NOW rule on Home's Coming up, Home's To do and the To do page (it is what makes overdue obvious), the Late 3 tab, the numbered setup list and the 13-14px text floor. FIX: ship the Late filter for real (add a 'late' status to routes.tasks), or the tab will not work. On Home, drop or shrink the 'Next in 2 days' tube to one line, since the rail's lit stop 1 already says it, and give the width back to the box. On To do and Ideas at 1280, narrow the figure gutter (Fig. 1 legend plus counters) to about 220px, or move it above the list on the phone, so the list's Edit buttons are not pushed to the edge. On Plans Month, close the 90px gap beside the gauge.

KEEP the readout strip, the box-first greeting, the two-line caution with its link, and the plain square checkboxes. FIX: make each readout cell a link (Plans 4 to /plans, Late 3 to To do filtered late, Ideas 12 to /ideas) with a 44px target. Put the next plan back as row 1 of Coming up's list (marked 'Next'), so the list is complete without the tube. Shorten the arcs band to about 60px, or label each stop with the plan's name on hover and focus, so it is a way in and not only decoration. On the phone, keep the readout cells on the first screen.

KEEP Home as the map (each page a panel with a count and a link), To do's Who/Due columns, Settings' 'Needs a look' first, and the household row. FIX: set the question in Plex at full bone or white with only 'plan' in VT323 green, since VT323 at 2.8rem is harder to read than plain type for tired eyes. On the phone, show all three starters as a wrapping row instead of hiding two. Let To do's panel shrink to its rows, or fill the gap with 'Next due', so no empty graphite reads as 'nothing loaded'. Find and fix the one target under 44px on Home.

KEEP the big day numeral that leads each Coming up row and matches the waypoint ring and the month cell: it is the best date scan in the heat. Keep the crew filter on To do. FIX: put back square checkboxes for ticking. A round pilot lamp may sit beside a row as state, but the thing you press to mark done must look like a box, here and on the form's 'Needs booking' and 'Send where I am'. Make the crew filter a real owner parameter, so the counts follow it.

KEEP the two-line Caution strip, and the rule that every figure mark links to its row, which lands lit. FIX Fig. 0: write the full names (Sam, Alex, Maya, Theo), not single letters, and on the phone collapse it to one line ('Alex spoke last · 4 plans · 3 late'), so the box and the lists are not pushed below a picture. Make sure its terminals ('4 to do · 3 late') are 44px links. Return the title to 'Tell Vera what to plan.'

KEEP the starter keys that name where they land (→ Plans, → To do, → Ideas): they teach the app's map at the point of use, so carry them into the refine. FIX: raise 'What's the' to full-contrast ink, remove the hatched empty box beside Status, and keep Row 0 to one line or break it without a trailing separator.

b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure refine and mutant). It is an imperative a first-timer can act on: it names who hears you and the job, and it reads as an instruction for the box beneath it, with the lit word last. Second: 'What's our plan?' (console refine). It is warm, in the family's 'our', and short on a phone, but as a question it can read as 'show me our plan', which makes it slightly less clear that you are meant to type. 'Tell Vera our plan.' (console graft) is clear but a little stiff. 'Tell Vera our plans.' (figure graft) presumes the plans already exist and suits ideas and reminders less well. 'What are we planning?' (console mutant) is fine but longer, and asks rather than invites. 'What's the plan?' (switchboard refine and graft) is the weakest for a box you write into: it reads as a request for information, the skeptic's 'show me the plan', and in dim VT323 it is also the hardest to read. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard mutant) is a yes/no question, which invites 'no'.

b.notes: Grafts that worked: the waypoint day numeral in Waypoint Lamps unifies Home, the route and the month, and is the best system move in the heat. Fig. 0 in Wired Household finally draws the household and gives Home a figure from its own data. The patch keys in Patched Through tie each starter to its page. Grafts that failed: Waypoint Lamps' tick lamps (an amber minus reads as delete or warning), the placards (decoding text where the design should be self-evident), Patched Through's dashed block caps and dead hatched cell, and Wired Household's green '3 late' chip, which contradicts its own colour rule. Every lineage still reaches for inverted-green chips (Today, Working, 3 late): glare and an editor-theme tic that should go everywhere. Switchboard's graphite panels keep a greyed ground, and its green share stays high (58–73%). Its inner pages waste the rack, the chat worst. The dice mutants of this round are near-duplicates (Squared, Magazine) or clip art (Drawn). Relighting the tubes worked best in figure refine and console graft, where the light sits on the monitors and the next item, not across the page.

scores.why: Green on black everywhere, a green-tinted ground and green chips on everything; it is the Matrix the family named, with no grounded colour to rest the eye.
A calm, coherent desk with a real tube, but its Home is cramped panels of small mono type, and Plans and To do are flat tables, so it reads as an editor theme more than a page.
The rails and the bone-on-green-black type are sound. The tube is a duplicate Next up, and the figure panels leave dead grid space beside their rows.

The best-set page in the heat: bone display heads, a lit NOW rail that touches its rows, real tubes on Home, Plans and Status, and amber kept to late. Faults: Fig. 1's grid box is half empty above the rail, To do's 'Now' sits at a different height from Coming up's, and on Plans the gauge and the Next line say the same thing twice.

Fig. 0 is the boldest new picture here and it carries real data, but its bare S/A/M/T initials are cryptic. '3 late' is lit as an inverted green chip, which breaks the lineage's own amber-means-late rule. The amber 'Caution' ring reads as a warning costume over a routine setup step.

The light sentence-case heads look elegant on the sheet, but they lose mass on the squint, and the semibold rows and green key now outweigh the heads. Beyond type it is a near-duplicate of its parent, so it gives little that the owner's 'reflect the page content' test can see.
The flight plan and the readout strip are a real structure, but the route reads violet and decorative, and the box competes with the tube for the lead.

The leader readout rail is clear and the slate-cyan route is calm. The list skips the next plan (rows 1–3 start at the 9th, while the Next ring has no number), which is a mismatch a reader will trip on. The inverted-green 'Fri 2 Oct' chip is glare, and the amber setup slab is louder than it needs to be.

The most coherent system in the heat. One day numeral runs through the row, the waypoint ring and the month cell. The route is bone on slate, and every page has one tube with a placard. Faults: the tick lamps show an amber minus that reads as 'remove' or a warning rather than a checkbox. Status's inverted-green 'Working' tags are an editor-theme tic. The placards over-explain, and the light day numerals beside mono ring numerals make two faces for one mark.
Clip art: a hard-coded Pacific Northwest landscape behind the words of the box, and violet decoy legs that look like data but match nothing. The other pages are near-duplicates of the parent.
The videotex map is a real idea, but the panels are grey graphite (a greyed ground), the dim VT323 is muddy, and green is 71% of the colour.

Home is the tidiest map in the lineage: Plans gets its own radar, To do's rows are clean, and the household strip at the foot is good. The inner pages waste the rack: the chat is a narrow column in a huge empty pane, and To do's list fills only a quarter of the screen. The graphite panels still tint the ground grey, and amber outlines on the late checkboxes shout.

Keying each starter to the page it lands on is a good idea. But 'What's the' is set in dim green VT323 that smears, there is a hatched dead cell in the household rack, the dashed separated-block caps add noise everywhere, and Ideas leaves an empty well.
A near-duplicate of Switchboard, Patched: squared lamps are invisible at page scale, it is greener than its parent (73%), and its leaders are faint again.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the one day numeral (row, waypoint ring, month cell), the bone route on slate, the one-tube-per-page grammar and the amber 3px late edge. Fix To do and Home's ticks: draw an empty square or ring that fills on done, with lateness carried by the row edge and the words, never by an amber minus inside the tick. On Status, replace the inverted-green 'Working' and 'off' tags with a lamp and plain dim words. Cut each placard to one short line, or fold it into the tube's caption. Set the ring numerals in the same face as the row numerals. Fill the empty ground right of Coming up's relative column, or narrow the bay.

Keep the bone display heads, 'Tell Vera what to plan.', the lit NOW rail touching its rows, and the round tubes. Fix Fig. 1 on Home: crop the grid box to the rows, since its empty upper third reads as a blank panel. Put To do's 'Now' at the same height as Coming up's NOW, or drop one of them. On Plans, either drop the 'Next' line or make the gauge name the plan, and close the ~90px gap beside the gauge. Join the month's NOW across Mon–Thu so it does not read as a broken trace.

Keep Fig. 0 (the household wired to Vera, the lit wire of whoever spoke last, terminals with live counts); it is the lineage's best new picture. Write the members' names, or monogram plus name, instead of bare S/A/M/T. Make '3 late' amber, not inverted green: green is live, amber is late. Replace the amber 'Caution' ring on the setup line with the refine's numbered steps, since a routine step should not look like an alarm. Keep one NOW per screen.

Keep the leader readout rail and the slate-cyan route. Number the next plan as 1 and list it in the rows as well as in the tube (or drop the tube's duplicate), so the rings and the rows agree. Make 'Today' plain bone with a lit dot, not an inverted green chip. Make the setup bay a thin amber edge, not a slab with a lamp block.

Keep the Home map (Plans with its own radar, the household strip, the clean To do table). Take the graphite panel fill down to the green-black ground with a 1px rule. Give the inner pages' lists the full width, and let the chat use its pane: the thread is a narrow column beside a large empty field. On late checkboxes use a neutral outline, with amber only on the edge and the words.

Keep the patch keys (each starter shows the page it lands on), a strong and usable idea worth grafting into other lineages. Set the title in Plex with only 'plan' lit, or set the whole VT323 title bright, never a dim smear. Remove the hatched dead cell. Replace the dashed block caps with one solid 2px cap. Close Ideas' empty well.

Drop the landscape and the violet decoy legs. If a picture stays, draw it from data (the real flight plan) and keep it out from under the text. The single-family arrowheads and the kind badges could be kept as small refinements.

b.titles: The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure refine and mutant). It names who hears you and the whole job in one imperative verb, reads as an invitation to tell her something, and lights the job word at the end of the line. Second is 'Tell Vera our plan.' (console graft): it is close, but 'our plan' slightly presumes a plan exists. 'Tell Vera our plans.' (figure graft) is the same with a plural that sits a little awkwardly. Weaker: 'What's our plan?' and 'What's the plan?' read as asking the app to SHOW the plan, a query rather than an invitation to tell, and Switchboard Patched Through sets 'What's the' in a dim smear. 'What are we planning?' (console mutant) is fine but generic. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard mutant) is a yes/no question that invites 'no'. The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.'; the runner-up is 'Tell Vera our plan.'
